title: CD Projekt Red uses AI (Respeecher), with consent, to match Jacek Rozenek's new Polish Geralt lines in Witcher 3: Songs of the Past (report)
game: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt (Songs of the Past)

sources.note: Insider Gaming 11 Nov, citing Stephen Totillo's Game File interview with CDPR reps; Rozenek and Szwed quotes
Game File, paywalled, not read; origin of the report
CDPR press, 25 Aug: Songs of the Past paid expansion, 2027, PC PS5 Xbox Series X|S Switch 2, with Fool's Theory

first_report: 2026-11-11 Game File (time not read); Insider Gaming 23:38 Dubai (19:38Z) per the 23:48 digest

claims.claim: Respeecher used to match Rozenek's new Polish Geralt lines to his earlier voice, with his consent
Rozenek records the new lines himself; voice changed after a 2019 stroke
English Geralt (Doug Cockle) not given the same treatment
Songs of the Past launches in 2027

gate: gate 22:45Z: Insider read in full, CDPR press page read, web search found no denial and no CDPR statement; Game File paywalled; runs as تقرير

angle.hook: the Polish Geralt actor still records his own lines, but AI makes them sound like his voice from before his stroke
angle.why_now: Game File published the interview on 11 Nov and Insider Gaming relayed it hours ago, a few months after CD Projekt announced the Songs of the Past expansion for 2027
angle.what_it_means_here: Voice actors and dubbing are a live debate for Arabic gamers too, and here the studio says the actor consented and still performs the lines
angle.payoff: the studio calls it an ethical use with consent, and the English Geralt is not processed
